newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end lower on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end lower on fund selling.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures ended lower on a fund exodus tied to bearish technical indicators and ideas the four-month rally in soymeal was faltering, traders said.
Floor sources noted technical signals remained bearish after Monday's sharp break. Funds sold at least 3,000 lots soymeal and 1,200 lots soyoil on the day.

Soymeal had been bolstered by a lack of deliveries against the May contract which expires next week and the tight basis levels in the cash market. But some suggested the July would not be able to hold up after the May went off the board.
Market talk circulated that traders holding positions in the May meal contract had received phone calls requesting that they liquidate positions ahead of expiry next Tuesday.
"The talk is there were a few 'hand on the back' calls placed last night to people still in the May," a floor trader said. "Nothing forceful yet, just a nudge."
CBOT said the open interest in the May was 5,428 lots as of Tuesday, down 1,455 from the previous day.
Soymeal ended $1.80 to $0.50 per ton lower with July off $1.80 at $288.90. Soyoil closed 0.47 to 0.32 cent per lb lower with July off 0.36 at 23.88.
On the day, funds sold at least 3,000 lots soymeal and 1,200 lots soyoil.
In soymeal, Merrill Lynch sold 1,000 lots July and 200 December while LIT sold 600 July.
In soyoil, CIS sold 450 lots July and Lee B. Stern sold 400 July.
Soymeal volume was estimated by CBOT 34,000 contracts, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 28,766. Soyoil volume was pegged at 20,000 lots, against Tuesday's 15,000.
